citation: Thurner, L., Scheidler, A., Schäfer, F., Menke, J., Dollichon, J., Meier, F., Meinecke, S., Braun, M. (2018). pandapower: An Open-Source Python Tool for Convenient Modeling, Analysis, and Optimization of Electric Power Systems. IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 33(6), 6510-6521. doi:10.1109/TPWRS.2018.2829021
description: pandapower is an open-source Python program for the automated analysis and optimisation of electric power systems. It is a joint development of the Department for Sustainable Electrical Energy Systems (e2n) at the University of Kassel and the Department for Distribution System Operation at the Fraunhofer Institute for Energy Economics and Energy System Technology (IEE) in Kassel. Networks are held as pandas tables of buses, lines, transformers, switches, loads, generators, storage and controllers; the package implements balanced and three-phase power flow with an improved Newton-Raphson solver, optimal power flow, short-circuit calculation to IEC 60909, state estimation, contingency analysis, time series simulation, topology search, grid equivalents, protection and plotting. Alternative solvers include PYPOWER, PowerGridModel, lightsim2grid and PowerModels.jl, and HELMpy when installed separately; converters read MATPOWER and PYPOWER cases, CIM CGMES, PowerFactory exports and, since version 3.5.0 (July 2026), OpenDSS feeders, imported as balanced positive-sequence networks. It is generic and location independent, applicable to any network for which parameters exist. Distribution is through PyPI (version 3.5.5, 22 September 2026, Python 3.10 or newer), the GitHub repository, pandapower.org and read-the-docs documentation, under the BSD-3-Clause licence at no cost. Caveats: it is a steady-state tool without electromagnetic transients, and the SimBench benchmark grids and load profiles recommended for realistic studies are a separate package. Simulation uses are network flow, contingency and cascading failure analysis, capacity planning, optimisation and resilience studies. Related records: it imports feeders from OpenDSS, catalogued here as platform-opendss.
